A feature just shipped to production in the tetrix-game-monorepo (commits f9ba144 and 0490089 on master, frontend 7.72.0, 2026-08-20). Reflect it in the Opportunity Solution Tree.

What shipped:
- Campaign mode levels have their rules computed from the prime factors of the level number (admin binds (prime, exponent) → feature). Until now nothing described a level to the player. Now: generated "feature badges" (PNG art cut from the game's real block component per theme) describe each active rule — clear-lines (with ×N caption), point target (with N), random recolor, corner block (1x1/2x2/3x3/6x6-L, drawn from the engine's own blocked cells), empty-board secondary win, breather, backlog placeholder.
- Player surfaces: the Campaign pathway now shows a "level brief" (badges + one-sentence rules) for the upcoming level BEFORE the player commits, backed by GET /api/campaign/me carrying currentLevelConfig; the in-level HUD shows badges for bound pacing, hazards and the live secondary-win state.
- Admin: the campaign rule editor was cleaned up (compact rows with the player's badge, explicit "otherwise →" fallback row, collapsed add-rule form with live reach/conflict hint and badge preview). Admins see exactly what players will.
- Tests: unit (badge mapping + a guard that every badge id has PNGs on disk), backend pg test for /campaign/me, and a beta-stack Playwright spec that asserts the badge images actually decode in the production image.

Your job: read the tree first (ost_list_nodes / ost_get_node), find the opportunity/solution nodes this relates to (campaign mode, "I want to understand what a level asks of me" / legibility / progression-type opportunities, or the campaign solution node from the 7.70–7.71 work if one exists). Mark the relevant solution as shipped/live with evidence pointing at the commits, add a solution node for "badges describe a level's rules before and during play" under the right opportunity if none exists, and add the admin-editor cleanup as an annotation rather than a player-facing solution. If the tree has no campaign-related node at all, add the minimal honest structure (opportunity → solution) under the outcome and say so. Validate at the end (ost_validate). Report back exactly which nodes you created/updated with their ids, and anything you judged NOT to add and why.

# @tetrix/ost-mcp

An MCP server that manages an **Opportunity Solution Tree** (OST) — a
Teresa-Torres discovery map stored as a folder of one-node-per-Markdown-file —
and **enforces its structural invariants at the write boundary**. A malformed
edit is rejected with a structured `violations[]` list and nothing is written,
so the tree cannot rot. Same philosophy as this repo's `env.ts` and
`@tetrix/validation`: a rule that lives only in prose drifts; a validating tool
boundary cannot produce a bad node.

Reusable across products — point it at any OST folder.

## Node format

Each node is one `.md` file. Filename (minus `.md`) is the node's title and the
exact string other nodes link to.

```
#Opportunity
[[Shared-board co-op build mode]]
[[Live partner presence and shared cursors]]

Optional prose after the link region.
```

- **Line 1** is a single type tag: `#BusinessMetric`, `#Opportunity`,
  `#Solution`, or `#Assumption`.
- The **link region** (contiguous `[[...]]` lines under the tag) holds the
  *structural*, downward parent→child edges.
- Wikilinks embedded in **prose** are advisory, not structural edges.

## Configuration

| Source | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `OST_ROOT` (env) | Absolute path to the OST folder. **Required.** |
| `OST_OUTCOME` (env, optional) | Title of the root `#BusinessMetric`; auto-detected when exactly one exists. |
| `ost.config.json` in the root (optional) | Override `vocabulary`, `legalEdges`, or `outcome`. |

## Invariants

**Hard (writes rejected):**
- Exactly one valid type tag on line 1 (`missing-type`).
- Legal parent→child edges only (`illegal-edge`): `BusinessMetric→Opportunity`;
  `Opportunity→{Opportunity,Solution}`; `Solution→Assumption`; `Assumption`=leaf.
- No dangling structural links (`dangling-link`).
- No cycles (`cycle`).

**Warnings (reported by `ost_validate`, never block):** unreachable nodes
(`orphan`), missing/ambiguous outcome (`outcome`).

**Lints (opt-in via `ost_validate({ lint: true })`):** `unshipped`,
`no-solution`, `untested`.

## Tools

| Tool | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `ost_list_nodes` | All nodes: type, child links, shipped status. |
| `ost_get_node` | One node's parsed structure + raw content. |
| `ost_validate` | Full-tree audit. `{ lint?: boolean }`. |
| `ost_add_node` | Create a node + link it under its parent(s). |
| `ost_link` / `ost_unlink` | Add / remove one structural edge. |
| `ost_update_node` | Edit body prose and/or retype a node. |
| `ost_rename_node` | Rename + rewrite every inbound wikilink. |
| `ost_delete_node` | Delete; refuses to orphan children unless `reparent`/`cascade`. |

Every mutating tool validates the **whole proposed tree** before touching disk
and returns `{ ok: true, changes }` or `{ ok: false, violations }`.

> **Note:** `shipped` is a *derived, read-only* signal parsed from Solution
> prose (and the `unshipped` lint). Set shipped status by editing the body via
> `ost_update_node` — the server does not rewrite status sentences for you.

## Usage

```bash
pnpm --filter @tetrix/ost-mcp build
OST_ROOT="/path/to/OST" node packages/ost-mcp/dist/server.js   # stdio MCP server
```

Registered for Claude Code in the repo-root `.mcp.json` (server key `ost`) and
driven by the `ost-steward` agent (`.claude/agents/ost-steward.md`).

Use when shipping a feature that should be reflected in the discovery map, when a stubbed solution goes live, when code work implies a new user need, or when you want the tree audited. tools: Read, mcp__ost__ost_list_nodes, mcp__ost__ost_get_node, mcp__ost__ost_validate, mcp__ost__ost_add_node, mcp__ost__ost_link, mcp__ost__ost_unlink, mcp__ost__ost_update_node, mcp__ost__ost_rename_node, mcp__ost__ost_delete_node
---

You are the steward of this product's Opportunity Solution Tree (OST) — the
living Teresa-Torres discovery map linking a business outcome to the user
opportunities it depends on, the solutions that address them, and the
assumptions those solutions rest on.

## How you work

- **Every mutation is an `ost_*` tool call. Never hand-edit node files** — you do
  not have `Write`/`Edit` on the vault, and that is deliberate. The `ost-mcp`
  server enforces the tree's structural invariants (one type tag per node, legal
  parent→child edges, no dangling or cyclic links, filename↔title identity). Your
  job is to decide *what* to change; the server decides whether it is *legal*.
- **Read before you write.** Start from `ost_list_nodes` (and `ost_get_node` for
  detail) to understand the current tree before proposing a change.
- **When a write is refused,** the result is `{ ok: false, violations: [...] }`.
  Read the violations, fix the cause (wrong parent type, missing node, would-be
  cycle), and retry — do not try to force it.
- **After a batch of changes, run `ost_validate`** and report any warnings
  (orphans) to the user. Pass `lint: true` only when the user asks for a
  discovery-health review (untested solutions, opportunities with no solution).

## The four node kinds and legal edges

- `#BusinessMetric` → `#Opportunity`
- `#Opportunity` → `#Opportunity` (sub-opportunities nest) or `#Solution`
- `#Solution` → `#Assumption`
- `#Assumption` is a leaf (it may *mention* solutions in prose, but that is not a
  structural edge)

Opportunity titles are first-person user statements ("I want to co-op with
friends"). Solution nodes note shipped status in their prose body
(set it via `ost_update_node`'s `body`).

## Common tasks

- **A feature shipped:** find or `ost_add_node` its `#Solution` under the right
  `#Opportunity`; note "Shipped." in the body via `ost_update_node`.
- **A stubbed solution went live:** `ost_update_node` its body to reflect shipped
  status.
- **Code work implies a new user need:** do **not** silently add an Opportunity —
  ask the user first, then `ost_add_node` it under the outcome.
- **Rename a node:** always use `ost_rename_node` so inbound links are rewritten;
  never delete-and-recreate.

2. **Likely cause: the server's default vault path is a typo.** `/Users/tanner/dev/tetrix-game-monorepo/.mcp.json` sets
   `OST_ROOT` to `${OST_ROOT:-/Users/tannerbrobers/Documents/Obsidian Vault/Discovery/Tetrix/OST}` — `tannerbrobers`, not `tanner`. Unless `OST_ROOT` is set in the launching environment, the server starts against a non-existent folder.
3. **I could not locate a vault at any candidate path.** Probed (both `ost.config.json` and the outcome node `10,000 daily, active, account holding users play in the tetrix ecosystem.md`) at:
   - `/Users/tanner/dev/tetrix-ost/` (the path my memory note says the vault was re-initialised at on 2026-07-26)
   - `/Users/tannerbrobers/Documents/Obsidian Vault/Discovery/Tetrix/OST/`
   - `/Users/tanner/Documents/Obsidian Vault/Discovery/Tetrix/OST/`
   None exist. Either the vault lives somewhere else now, or it was moved/deleted since July.
4. The server itself is built: `/Users/tanner/dev/tetrix-game-monorepo/packages/ost-mcp/dist/server.js` exists.

### To unblock

Set `OST_ROOT` to the real vault folder (or fix the default in `.mcp.json`), confirm the `ost` MCP server connects, then re-launch this task. Everything below is ready to execute the moment the tools are present.

### The change plan I will apply once connected

After `ost_list_nodes` / `ost_get_node` to confirm what actually exists, the intended mutations are:

- **Find the campaign `#Solution` from the 7.70–7.71 work** (prime-factored levels, admin rule editor). `ost_update_node` its body: "Shipped. Live in production as of frontend 7.72.0 (2026-08-20); see commits f9ba144, 0490089 on master." If it is still stubbed, this is the "stub went live" path.
- **Add one new player-facing `#Solution`** — working title *"Feature badges describe a level's rules before and during play"* — under the legibility/progression opportunity (something like "I want to understand what a level asks of me before I commit"). Body: badges are PNG art cut from the real block component per theme; covers clear-lines (×N), point target (N), random recolor, corner block (1x1/2x2/3x3/6x6-L from engine blocked cells), empty-board secondary win, breather, backlog placeholder; surfaced as a pre-commit level brief on the Campaign pathway (backed by `GET /api/campaign/me` → `currentLevelConfig`) and as in-level HUD badges for pacing, hazards and live secondary-win state. Shipped 7.72.0, commits f9ba144 / 0490089. Evidence: unit tests (badge mapping + every-badge-id-has-PNGs guard), backend pg test for `/campaign/me`, beta-stack Playwright spec asserting the images decode in the production image.
- **If no such opportunity exists**, I will add it under the outcome as the minimal honest structure (opportunity → the solution above) — and flag in the report that I added an Opportunity, since the steward rules say to ask first; given the parent agent's explicit instruction to do so if nothing campaign-related exists, I treat that instruction as the authorisation, but will call it out.

- Then `ost_validate` (no lint) and report orphan warnings.

### What I judged not to add (regardless of tool availability)

- **No separate solution for the test suites** (unit/pg/Playwright). Tests are evidence on the solution body, not solutions.
- **No `#Assumption` nodes yet.** The obvious one — "players who can read a level's rules before committing are more likely to start and finish campaign levels" — is worth testing, but I would rather see whether an existing assumption under the campaign solution already covers it before adding one, and it is not in the brief.
